fields.title: Typical Bottlenecks
fields.keyTakeaway: Most time in a product system goes to the number of calls, call sequence, and data size, and all of these are fixed by changing queries rather than speeding up code.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: Where does time usually go in a product system?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Knowing typical locations cuts search time from a week to an hour. Most performance problems repeat from product to product.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Six places where time usually hides, in order of frequency.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **Number of database calls.** [[n1-problem|The N+1 problem]]: a list of 50 items generates 50 queries. Symptom in tracing: many identical short segments. Fixed by batch loading.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Sequence of independent calls.** Waiting for one to start another even though there is no dependency. Symptom: a staircase in tracing. Fixed by parallelization.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Missing index.** One query taking 900 ms instead of 5. Covered in `DS1-N4-L2`.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Size of transferred data.** Fetching everything, displaying a part. Fixed by field selection and pagination.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **Client images.** Original sizes instead of prepared ones. Often the largest component on mobile.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: **Synchronous calls to external services on the critical path.** Someone else's time in our budget.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Practical analysis order: look at the trace, find the longest segment and repeating segments. Two minutes usually gives the answer.
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: Product takeaway: **the first, second, fourth, and sixth are fixed without code optimization**—they are solved by changing what is requested and when.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Inventory across six items on five main screens:
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Five screens, three days of analysis, about four seconds total. Not a single code optimization task—only changing what gets requested.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Order history turned out to be the heaviest screen even though nobody complained about it: it is opened rarely, and slowness was attributed to its rarity.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: The list of typical places does not replace measurement. It tells you where to look, not what you will find there.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Most time in a product system goes to the number of calls, call sequence, and data size, and all of these are fixed by changing queries rather than speeding up code.
